'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Colombian conflict]]
**[[2022 Arauca clashes]]
***Clashes between the [[revolutionary]] [[Far-left politics|far-left]] armed groups [[National Liberation Army (Colombia)|ELN]] and [[FARC dissidents]] in [[Arauca Department]] leave 23 people dead near [[Colombia]]’s [[Colombia-Venezuela border|border with]] [[Venezuela]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2022/1/3/colombia-at-least-16-dead-in-clashes-between-armed-rebel-groups (Al Jazeera)]
*[[Syrian civil war]]
**Five [[Syrian Army|soldiers]] are killed and 20 more are injured during an [[Islamic State]] [[rocket]] attack on a military transport bus in the [[Syrian Desert]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2022/1/3/five-syrian-soldiers-killed-20-injured-by-isil-state-media (Al Jazeera)]
*Spillover of the [[Somali Civil War (2009–present)|Somali Civil War]]
**Six men are killed by suspected [[Al-Shabaab (militant group)|al-Shabaab]] [[militant]]s in a village in [[Lamu County]], [[Kenya]], near the border with [[Somalia]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/africa/bodies-burnt-one-victim-beheaded-kenyan-village-near-somalia-police-2022-01-03/ (Reuters)]
*[[Yemeni Civil War (2014–present)|Yemeni Civil War]]
**[[Houthi movement|Houthi forces]] capture a [[United Arab Emirates]]-flagged cargo ship, the ''Rwabee'', off [[Al Hudaydah]], [[Yemen]]. The [[UAE government]] says that the vessel was carrying equipment from a closed [[Saudi Arabian-led intervention in Yemen|coalition]] [[field hospital]] on [[Socotra]] while the Houthis say that the vessel was carrying [[military equipment]]. [https://www.msn.com/en-gb/news/world/iran-backed-houthis-seize-uae-ship-on-anniversary-of-soleimani-assassination/ar-AASnZvR?ocid=BingNewsSearch (MSN)]

'''Business and economy'''
*[[Evergrande liquidity crisis]]
**[[China|Chinese]] [[property developer]] [[Evergrande Group]] suspends trading of its shares on the [[Hong Kong Stock Exchange]] ahead of a planned [[restructuring]] of the firm. [https://www.bbc.com/news/business-59855881 (BBC News)]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Asia]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in India]], [[COVID-19 vaccination in India]]
****[[India]] begins administering [[COVID-19 vaccine]]s for children between the ages of 15 and 18 years using the domestically produced [[Covaxin]] vaccine manufactured by [[Bharat Biotech]]. [https://www.hindustantimes.com/india-news/covid19-vaccination-of-children-aged-between-15-and-18-begins-today-101641167567261.html (''Hindustan Times'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the Philippines]], [[COVID-19 vaccination in the Philippines]]
****The [[Metropolitan Manila Development Authority#Metro Manila Council|Metro Manila Council]] passes a resolution imposing a lockdown on all unvaccinated and partially vaccinated residents and minors due to an increase in the number of cases of the SARS-CoV-2 Omicron variant. [https://www.rappler.com/nation/unvaccinated-people-metro-manila-prohibited-going-outside/ (Rappler)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in South Korea]]
****[[South Korea]] reports its first confirmed deaths related to the SARS-CoV-2 Omicron variant in two people in their 90s who died last week at a senior care hospital in [[Gwangju]]. [https://en.yna.co.kr/view/AEN20220103004400315?section=national/national (Yonhap News Agency)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Taiwan]]
****[[Taiwan]] reports its first two locally transmitted cases of the SARS-CoV-2 Omicron variant. [https://www.taiwannews.com.tw/en/news/4396674 (''Taiwan News'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Europe]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United Kingdom]]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in Scotland]]
*****[[Scotland]] reports a record 20,217 new cases of COVID-19 in the past 24 hours. [https://www.independent.co.uk/news/uk/scottish-government-covid-scottish-parliament-first-minister-msps-b1985927.html (''The Independent'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Belgium]], [[COVID-19 drug development]]
****The [[Belgium|Belgian]] [[Government of Belgium|government]] finalizes an agreement to buy 20,000 courses of [[Pfizer]]'s [[Paxlovid]] COVID-19 drug and [[Merck & Co.]]'s [[Molnupiravir]] COVID-19 drug. [https://www.brusselstimes.com/health/200187/belgium-orders-20000-covid-19-pills-for-serious-symptoms (''The Brussels Times'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in France]]
****[[France]] begins to require children over the age of 6 years to wear [[Face masks during the COVID-19 pandemic|mask]]s while indoors and also reduces the self-isolation period for fully [[COVID-19 vaccination in France|vaccinated]] people to seven days and five days if a person has received a negative [[Polymerase chain reaction|PCR]] or antigen test due to a record number of COVID-19 cases driven by the [[SARS-CoV-2 Omicron variant]]. [https://thehill.com/policy/international/europe/587885-france-orders-indoor-masking-for-children-six-and-older (''The Hill'')] [https://www.politico.eu/article/france-quarantine-isolation-vaccinated-omicron/ (''Politico.eu'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Mozambique]]
***[[President of Mozambique|President]] [[Filipe Nyusi]] and his wife [[Isaura Nyusi|Isaura]] test positive for COVID-19. [https://www.news24.com/amp/news24/africa/news/mozambique-president-and-wife-test-positive-for-covid-19-20220103 (''News24'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United States]], [[COVID-19 vaccination in the United States]]
***The [[Food and Drug Administration]] authorizes the use of the [[Pfizer–BioNTech COVID-19 vaccine]] as a [[booster dose]] for children between the ages of 12 and 15 years, becoming the world's first vaccine to be authorized as a booster shot for this age group. [https://abcnews.go.com/Health/fda-authorizes-pfizer-covid-19-boosters-12-15/story?id=82051567 (ABC News)]

'''Science and technology'''
*[[Cyberwarfare and Iran]]
**The website of [[Israel]]'s ''[[The Jerusalem Post|Jerusalem Post]]'' newspaper is hacked by suspected [[Iran]]ian hackers. The website's content was replaced with a threat targeting the [[Shimon Peres Negev Nuclear Research Center]] and an apparent reference to [[Qasem Soleimani]], who was [[Assassination of Qasem Soleimani|assassinated]] exactly two years earlier in [[Baghdad]], [[Iraq]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/israels-jerusalem-post-website-hacked-soleimani-assassination-anniversary-2022-01-03/ (Reuters)]
